text_fidelity_a:
Gaiam Total Body Balance Ball Kit - Includes Anti-Burst Stability Exercise Yoga Ball, Air Pump, Workout Program For sitting long periods of time on the ball, going a size up is a good idea, but I have found that you want to stick with your size for the stretches and workouts to get the most out of them. For instance, I am 5'4" or 5'5" and definitely need to go back and buy the smaller ball for the workouts. But I prefer either the 65" or the 75" for sitting for any period of time. Getting two sizes is a really worthwhile investment, imo. I always sit on a ball or on a balance cushion (when not in a recliner) b/c of hip and back issues, and it makes SUCH a difference. [[UPDATE: the 55" is way too small for me. It seems what I'd really need are two 65" w/ one of them far less inflated for doing the workout... sigh]]

I had problems w/ the DVD from the go--it was a mess even though it wasn't scratched. The part I could see I really liked, but with medical disabilities, it was a little too hard on my body anyhow (do not underestimate the after-effects of swinging a ball full of air over your head--lol--amazing workout!). When I contacted Gaiam about the DVD, they sent me a replacement. Happily, it was different one that was more suited to my health, a beginner's workout done by a blonde woman named Suzanne. It consists of 45 minutes of mostly stretches. I've done it every day for a week, and my chiropractor cannot believe the difference in my spinal health and other parts of my body as well--even my g.i. So score for Gaiam as a company and for their videos! It may seem like a long time to just stretch (w/ a modicum of strength and toning), but it is proving to be so worth it.

As for the videos that come with this ball, they consist of far less stretching and more aerobic strengthening from what I can tell. I really like the woman who leads them.

I had problems getting any of the three plugs that came with the ball into the ball. The hole really was not shaped properly. I solved this by substituting the somewhat smaller plug from my balance cushion until I had stretched the hole out sufficiently. I realize, however, that not all of you will have another plug lying around and so thought I should mention that. Probably if you jammed the plug as far as it would go and sat on the ball for a few days w/o exercising, it would stretch out and go into the hole.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Total Body Balance Ball Kit - Includes Anti-Burst Stability Exercise Yoga Ball, Air Pump, Workout Program

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Inspire HR Heart Rate and Fitness Tracker With S and L Bands, White, One Size, 1 Count Brand new out of the box, trying to set it up, and this thing is already presenting challenges. If you're thinking of getting one here's what you need to know: the charger is magnet so it attracts the charging prongs to the device easily HOWEVER, the magnet isn't strong enough to hold onto the device. If you set it down, it pops off the charging cord. You have to lay it down, propped on something, veeeerrrrrry carefully. I haven't even worn this thing and I can see that this is going to drive me nuts!!! I may deploy some high tech hacks - like a twist tie or some masking tape - to content with the charger design. :-p I'll come back and write more once I've set up and worn this thing.

You should know, I"m a devoted fitbit user and wear my devices out - they retire off to wherever beloved exhausted devices go after their life ends. I'm so sad my Alta HR died. I want it back! I still have my old Flex as a backup. I've never considered buying another brand of tracker and probably never will.

2/8/2020 - I'm back and I've upgraded stars from 3 to 5. The magnetic charger thing is still a bummer but absolutely everything else about this tracker is phenomenal. I can't believe this thing has so many features at its price point. Interaction with the screen is intuitive. The features available on-screen are a step up from the Alta HR. There's a Breath/relax/meditation function, a Timer, you can view and enable/disable the silent alarm settings right on the device, you can see how many steps you have left to meet the Reminder To Move target. I simply ADORE this thing!!! Fitbit, you really brought it with this tracker. I thank you.

7/7/2020 Back again with more information. Exactly 6 months after purchase, the device won't sync so I tried pairing it again to Bluetooth. The device won't pair so I tried resetting it per Fitbit product help web pages. The device won't reset. Now what? I loved the features on this device but it's hard to love something that won't work. Back to 3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Inspire HR Heart Rate and Fitness Tracker With S and L Bands, White, One Size, 1 Count

text_fidelity_a:
Eberlestock Phantom Pack This is far and away the finest pack I've ever used. Basically a Halftrack with the addition of a removable scabbard.
Quality of construction is top notch pretty much everywhere. That's a good thing, because there are zippers in several key areas, which I consider a strategic weakness. The scabbard zips to the main ruck, with spring clips at the top. The zippers each have a little hook that they catch on to keep them from accidentally riding up and the scabbard coming loose -- very nicely done. The handles are very sturdy, and well placed. PALS webbing is very useful, and well placed. I have several pouches of assorted types in various places. I'm extremely happy with this pack.

Minor beefs:
-The shoulder straps are far apart, designed for guys with a large frame. I'm a bit on the small side, and it's uncomfortable if I don't have the front clip pulled tight to keep the shoulder straps closer together.
-The belt only attaches to the scabbard, and without the scabbard it's shoulder straps only.
-the bottom of the scabbard hangs down without a reliable means of pulling it up out of the way when not in use. I've tried folding mine up, but it doesn't stay. Not a big deal, but it should have some sort of hook or clip like the Scabbard's zippers do.
-Zippers form the critical connectors in several points, with no backup if they fail. Granted, these are some tough zippers, but I've seen tough zippers fail before. I have a half dozen very nice, heavy duty packs with zippers that have failed. I like the utility of the zipper, but it needs some contact points for a backup -- even just putting PALS webbing all along the zipper surfaces would allow field expedient 550 cord securement, though you could argue that the addition of such potential snag points increases the likelihood of zipper failure due to catastrophic hang-ups.
text_fidelity_b: Eberlestock Phantom Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Drop + Dan Durston X-Mid Tent – Ultralight, Double Walled, Backpacking and Thru Hiking Shelter, Simple Pitch, Fully Waterproof, Supported by Trekking Poles This is the lightest tent I've ever had. My back is broken. I can't carry hardly anything. But at a pound and a half, I can finally carry my own tent. And it's so easy to put up. Most trekking pole tents require you to estimate the stake placement and possibly have you move the stakes multiple times (I'm in the desert with hard rocky ground, no way.) They also require multiple guylines just to keep it upright. Not this tent. 4 to 6 stakes, two poles... good night. The washers to protect the ultralight weight fabric from the trekking poles was a long time coming in the camping world. A vestibule large enough to cook in. Built in guy outs. Huge vents.... that you can open and close... from the INSIDE! You can clip and unclip the inner tent from the outer... from inside the tent! And lastly, when its raining you have THE ABILITY TO PUT UP YOUR OUTER TENT AND INNER TENT FROM THE OUTSIDE. Keeping your sleep area dry.
It's ultralight and it sets up ultra fast. And it's the most affordable tent in its class, but, in my opinion, they created a class all their own. I've never seen a single tent do so much, weigh so little, and be so affordable. I think its going to be my forever tent.
text_fidelity_b: Drop + Dan Durston X-Mid Tent – Ultralight, Double Walled, Backpacking and Thru Hiking Shelter, Simple Pitch, Fully Waterproof, Supported by Trekking Poles

ZG Mask Active Carbon Filters Anti-dust Mesh Half Face Mask (Orange, XL) Wow! I love this mask! I've tried a few different masks, and most of them don't fit very well on my nose. Usually I don't get a tight seal around my nose with other masks, and I end up blowing air into my eyes. But, this mask is awesome! It forms a great seal around my nose, and this filters the way that it's supposed to. I think that part of this is the kind of double filter. The outside filter is the cloth of the mask, and then there's a high quality replaceable filter inside. And, it comes with an extra inside filter, which is great.

This makes it so easy for me to breathe when it's really dusty or when I'm walking down a city road with tons of pollution and exhaust. I think it's fashionable, too. The mouth part sticks out a bit, but I like that so that my face isn't squished. You could probably even suck a lollipop while wearing this, if you wanted.

I really like how the straps strap around my neck. That makes it so that it's a much better fit than just wrapping around my ears. They fit really snugly for me, so if you have a really big head and neck, then this might be a tight fit. I got the XL size, and that fit me perfectly. I would have said that I have an L-sized head, but I really don't know how to size heads. Overall, this is awesome!

*ZG gave me this mask to review*

text_fidelity_a: E-Z UP Camping Cube 6.4, Converts 10' Straight Leg Canopy into Camping Tent, Punch I took this on a camping trip and can honestly stay I will never have a tent that you can't stand up in ever again. This tent is awesome, it was so nice to be able to stand up straight and handle two kids in this tent. I was able to fit two oversized twin cots in this tent with a few feet at the bottom and a walkway down the middle. This tent is like the Tardis, its not so huge you can't find a place for it, but once you walk inside you are amazed at how much room you get. Its fantastic that you can use every inch of this tent with the 6 foot plus height in the entire tent. It was up in a matter of minutes with two people. I never again have to mess with tent poles SOOO HAPPY! The stakes are really heavy duty with this tent. I really need to buy a few more to use for the canopy that goes over the tent. I didn't get the same brand for the canopy that you need over the top of the tent. I ended up buying ABC brand Canopy, straight legged 10x10. And it works great for it. The tent has two straps in the top middle one for canopies with no low cross bars in the middle and one for low cross bars. Word of warning, do not attach the small black clips to the top of the canopy before using the Velcro straps around the canopy legs. If its windy it could break one of the black plastic clips. I wish the zipper was a little easier for opening and closing, but its heavy duty and serves its purpose. I will say the little welcome mat was a nice surprise. For cold nights its really kept the damp cold air out. Tent was at least 10-15 degrees warmer inside then outside at night. Yes its a little heavier than other tents, but for adults with Kids this is a must! You can also buy accessories with this tent, I bought a collapsible corner shelf. And there is a hook in the middle of the tent for a light etc. Works really well, very well thought out with the oversized doors and windows.

text_fidelity_a:
Topeak Explorer Rack I will first say the build quality of the rack seems good, and if you can get it mounted correctly to your specific bike, it will likely be a good rack for you.

However the rack could have been designed to fit more bikes better with a little more forethought. The product description says this rack is 16 x 14.5 x 9 inches. Maybe it is, however the critical dimension is the length of the support post for tire clearance reasons. The distance from the center of the bolt hole on the bottom, to the bent bar on top - ie the clearance measurement - is 14 and 15/16 inches. A 29er tire radius is obviously 14.5 inches, so if you were to mount the bottom of this level with your axle bolt you would have only 7/16 inch clearance - less than half an inch. Most rack mounting holes are well above the axle point, but some are not much. I was using P-clips since my frame has not rack holes, and even though I was completely free to mount wherever I wanted, I had trouble finding a usable position with much clearance. Since most 29ers are used in the mud at least on occasion, a little more clearance would have been nice.

Secondly, the hardware included is stainless M5 x 0.8, and there are just enough assuming your frame has the proper mounting holes. If your using P-clips or any other method, a trip to the hardware store will be required, and you likely won't find stainless hardware in metric. It wouldn't have killed them to add an extra bag of hardware for other bike mounting methods.

Lastly, if you plan to use the Topeak accessories for mounting then the top of the rack will be great for you. If your not, the top of the rack is not flat like most racks (because of the MTX grooves for easy accessory mounting). If your not using topeak bags and such, you should still be able to make it work fine, its just not flat.

Unfortunately there aren't many racks out there yet for 29ers, so this still might be a good fit for many.
text_fidelity_b: Topeak Explorer Rack

The Fridge Drink Cooler - Lifoam If you like cold drinks, this is the ultimate coozie to get! They not only keep your drinks cold for hours, but they can actually make your drinks colder than they were from the refrigerator!

That is because each coozie has two main layers that work together to chill the drinks: an inner gel layer and a thick outer styrofoam layer.

When you put the coozie in the freezer, the gel layer freezes. This layer can actually drop the temperature of whatever drink you put int the coozie. It's like wrapping your drink in a blanket of ice! Then the styrofoam layer makes sure all that great coldness stays there. Drinks normally stay cold for several hours!

Another nice feature when using these coozies is that there is no problem with leaving wet rings on the furniture because the coozies prevent the normal condensation problem you have with cold drinks in a warm environment. I think this is because of the thick insulation layer. The cold inside is insulated from the warm outside which prevents condensation.

I know these coozies last for years. I originally found these coozies on MisterCold.com in 2006 and used them constantly ever since. I have taken them with me everywhere I go. They have held up very well for so much use. After 7 years of use, they finally began to show signs of wear (slight fraying at the bottom) so I decided it was time to get new ones. I was thrilled to find them here on Amazon! The new ones I got are just as good, if not better, than the original ones I bought years ago.

If you want to enjoy drinks that are cold, cold, cold and stay that way for hours, this is the perfect item for you. Just be sure to get a bunch because once your family and friends try them, they'll use them all the time. So you need plenty on hand to be sure there's always a cold one waiting for you! The rule in my house is you can use them as long as you don't take the last one. That way there's always at least one chilled and ready to go!
text_fidelity_b: The Fridge Drink Cooler - Lifoam

text_fidelity_a:
Tour Edge Men's TGS Triple Grind Sole Wedge Keep in mind I received it today and haven't used it much, but I did hit some side by side shots with my CG16 wedge of the same loft. Distance was virtually identical. I definitely saw the Tour launched the ball higher. I'm sure that's related to the spin increase compared to a 10 year old wedge. That being said, I certainly don't have any complaints.

I really like the grind. I was able to play with some knock downs from tight lies, hit full shots from the back and front of my stance, even hit a few wide open flops (yeah I know a 52 really isn't the club). In all cases I was able to make clean contact.

The feel isn't what I would call "pure", but it was fine. A bit clicky to me, but as far as my game goes I am not going to consider that a negative. Some more accomplished players may see that as a bad thing.

The lie isn't right for me, I seemed to pull most shots with a slight draw. The opposite of my current clubs as I normally fade them. We will see how that plays on the course, but that's on me, not the club.

Bottom line: Let's face it, a functional club for an extremely affordable price is something we all can use. This club fits the situation perfectly.
text_fidelity_b: Tour Edge Men's TGS Triple Grind Sole Wedge

Fitbit Wireless Activity/Sleep Tracker, Black/Plum After a couple of months, I find the Fitbit useful as a daily tracker of my relative activity levels. I'm not convinced at all of its estimates of calories burned, and since you don't manually enter your step length, I'm not sure how accurate it is on that score either. However, watching relative differences day to day seems like a very useful benefit.
I had been especially interested in the sleep monitoring function, but find it pretty useless. First, the arm band needed to hold the Fitbit as you sleep is uncomfortable if adjusted tightly enough to be sure it stays on. Second, the relative sleep quality it "calculates" differs significantly from my own perception of how well I slept. Even a very bad night (in my view) rated 97%! I no longer bother with it at night. Perhaps I don't understand how to use it most effectively.
Initially I had thought I'd order another for my wife once I tried it out. Now, I'm not sure it's worth the price to have two.

Moultrie Digital Picture Viewer, Black, 2 x 6 x 8.25 I like the viewer pretty well overall. I will tell you what I like first. It's fairly compact. The rubber grip surfaces make it easier to hold. I like that it has uses 4 AAA batteries. Devices with 4 batteries USUALLY have very long battery life, in my experience. It appears that all the covers to the buttons and hatches, etc, are water resistant and maybe waterproof. I like the positive slide on-off "click" of the power button. I love that I can leave one 16gb flashcard internal, and plug in a 2nd flashcard, and then without looking at any of the pictures, transfer everything off the 2nd card to the 1st card (assuming there's room), and then put the 2nd card back into the trail camera. That might be this viewer's best feature--the 2 SD card slots feature. The screen is adequate, altho I feel to really look at the pics, you should look at them on a laptop or desktop computer.

OK, here's what I don't like. I don't like the SD card sticking out of the bottom of the viewer. I would rather it be pressed into the slot and catch with the spring-loaded catch like the internal card slot, and be able to completely close the cover on the SD card. BUT, I realize they may have made it that way so you could take the card out with gloves on, cold fingers, etc. I also don't like how that rubber flap kinda hangs in the breeze when I peel it off to insert a card. text_fidelity_a:
Granite Ware 3 Qt Enamelware Coffee Boiler (Speckled Black) 12 Cups capacity - Ideal for Camping, Cabin, RV, Heat Coffee, Tea and Water directly on Stove or Fire. Dishwasher Safe. With only one coffee drinker in the family we didn't need a 3 quart coffee boiler for camp coffee. What we needed was an inexpensive, well built, 3-4 quart container for boiling water for cocoa, making coffee with a a one-cup Melita drip coffee cone, reconstituting instant oatmeal, and for easily adding hot water to our camp showers. The Graniteware coffee boiler was exactly what we needed. We fill it, use what we need for breakfast, then turn it off and set it aside. Later, especially if the day is cloudy or the solar shower water has cooled later in the evening, we'll add some more water, reheat, then add the hot water to our solar showers. We split it between two 2.5 gallon solar showers. The Graniteware Coffee Boiler was exactly what we needed and we've had absolutely no problems. Be sure to use a hot glove or pad when pouring if you just took it off the fire or the stove.

I also use it in my backyard for replenishing water in my smoker. I've learned the temperature of the smoker remains more constant when I add boiling water to the water reservoir. My gas grill has a separate pot burner and it is right next to my smoker. I just fill the coffee boiler with water, place it on the burner, and have hot water at the ready when I need to replenish the smoker.
text_fidelity_b: Granite Ware 3 Qt Enamelware Coffee Boiler (Speckled Black) 12 Cups capacity - Ideal for Camping, Cabin, RV, Heat Coffee, Tea and Water directly on Stove or Fire. Dishwasher Safe.

It also doesn't absorb water so it likes to float, but the diameter is small so with less weight it does get down to the bottom. Haven't really tested the tensile strength yet, but the "tug" test proved it was at least correct for the test weight that was listed. It also appears to be very clear. text_fidelity_a: DR.VIVA Fitness Tracker Watch, Heart Rate Activity Tracker Touch Color Screen IP67 Waterproof Sport Tracker Watch with Calorie Counter Pedometer Sleep Monitor for Kids Women Men I got this in exchange for my honest review.  This is a love hate relationship.  I love the features and all the different settings but I hate the interface.  Sometimes screens scroll super smooth and respond to touch inputs as they shoul and sometimes they wont scroll or lag so bad you want to smash this with a hammer.  Sometimes it links seamlessly with the phone and sometimes you canset it on top of the phone and it acts like it has never even haerd of bluetooth.  There is no rhyme or reason.  I used it in a workout yesterday and part way thru i must have bumped the screen because it turned off the fitness program.  Today it would not register i was working out at all.  Some of the data is super accurate (im wearing a second fitness watch just to compare) and some is so far off that according the the watch I may just be deceased (not really but i dont see my heartrate reaching 276 bpm just sitting watching videos)  The app is ok but does take some getting used to and some stuff that should be intuitive seems awkward and reversed.  They use odd terms for certian actions (like to unpair or disconnect from the phone they use the term unbind! )  There are a lot of nice features but are almost to specific (like there is no workout routine but you can choose tenmis, soccor, running, badmiton, basketball etc.).  And it stores messages (i thimk up to 5) but if you dont delete them new messages are not displayed only the old ones.  The band is real nice and the watch looks like a very expensive timepiece.  Charging was straight forward and batterylife was excellent.  The watch did get caught in an upgrade loop that kept telling us there was no devise connected.  We unbound and rebound the watch and it settled down.  There is a lot to do and set with this watch and when it is working it is really nice.  Patience is sometimes needed to work with it at times.  What i saw and used with this watch I really liked  and the app is a pretty good app once you get beyond some of awkward language

text_fidelity_a:
VENZO Compatible with Shimano SPD Mountain Bike CNC Cr-Mo Die-Cast Aluminum Sealed Pedals with Cleats - Dual Platform Clipless Pedals for Mountain Bike Shoes - Easy Clip in & Out I'm not really much of a bike rider, but lately I've been going on some longer trips (about 20 miles once a week or so) and decided that it might be worth my while to invest in some clip in pedals. After reading about the two main types of clipless systems, I decided the SPD-style pedals would better fit my bill and budget, and desire to stay around $100 together with shoes. Installation was a breeze, once I purchased an additional wrench to get my unexpectedly heavy old regular rectangle pedals off, and these Venzo brand pedals slipped right into place.

I haven't had any issues with the tension of the clipping mechanism after three solid rides so far, though I did have a bolt fall out of my shoe causing the shoe to get stuck clipped into the pedal -- I releasing the tension all the way got the shoe out but the small metal piece which the tension screw screws into is rather difficult to get back into position if it happens to fall out.

The included cleats fit nicely on the shoes I bought and other than some embarrassing falls and general awkwardness getting in/out of the pedals, I haven't had any issues with these pedals. If you are a beginning cyclist like myself looking for an affordable entry to clipless pedal systems, these fit the bill well. I also have taken some shorter trips with regular non clip-in shoes with these and they are acceptably fine.
text_fidelity_b: VENZO Compatible with Shimano SPD Mountain Bike CNC Cr-Mo Die-Cast Aluminum Sealed Pedals with Cleats - Dual Platform Clipless Pedals for Mountain Bike Shoes - Easy Clip in & Out

text_fidelity_a:
Old Bahama Bay Pop Up Beach Tent, Portable Shade Sun Shelter UPF50+ UV Protection for 4 Person Extendable Floor for Fishing Hiking Camping, Waterproof Windproof(Blue) [[VIDEOID:c0b9fb38604ef1dadcc1046c1f5ea08e]] We grabbed this Old Bahama Bay Pop Up Beach Tent for our beach days, where I have to be very careful not to overdo the sun. While she'll lay out, onto of time in the water, I try to get under shade when not out there. We do use umbrellas, but have struggled to find ways to provide consistent shade while the sun makes its track across the skies. So when I saw this...

1. It comes in a carrying bag that you'll use to store and, well, carry it. Like all such bags, the fit is tight. You'll pull to get it out, and be tested as with every such bag, and any box you have ever tried to repack things into - it's a chore. But it got in. We'd love to see such bags with another inch or so of space, but... Took two people pulling out, two people putting in. But as you can see in the video, my wife was able to pop it up alone.

2. There is a tie to keep it tight - think that tie around an umbrella. It would be really nice if this tie were another 4 inches, but you deal. It is not attached to anything, so you'll need to keep an eye on it.

3. The materials seem decent overall and the construction also decent. I'd say better than many ground clothes - which are mostly glorified tarps - but not as nice as some tents we've seen. It should give us a few years, or so our fingers will be crossed. Time will tell...

4. There are stakes and things we think are like shelves or pouches for inside the tent. We did not try them. But there are INSIDE the Old Bahama Bay Pop Up Beach Tent, wrapped and stuffed into that bag, so be careful when pulling things out - they are all apart of it, and as you do, you'll need to stuff them back inside. Not sure we'll use them, not sure we won't.

5. As you can see in the video... set up IS decently easy. Now that we've done it, it SHOULD be far easier when we get out to the beach next. My wife did it side-side-side-top and that worked. We talked about top first, but have not tried it yet. Taking it down was very similar, freaky a little easier now that she knew the strength it took and what would happen. Frankly, it's a cool design and works well. There is a "bottom" to it that's mainly a connected piece that you sort of unfold out and sticks out the front for an overlay onto the sand. It's a nice touch. Once out you can lay other ground clothes on it, blankets, whatever, and that should help hold it down. Again, there are stakes, but we did not try for this test.

We are hoping to get to the beach this upcoming weekend - weather permitting - so as soon as we do - if needed, we'd come back to update - but only if things don't go as planned. Not sure on the overall shade coverage, but the short period of time we were out there, the sun was directly over us and it did give us some decent shade. We feel like we'd set this up in combination with the umbrellas for an overall area of protection for me - and while we might leave the umbrellas in place, we'd move this Old Bahama Bay Pop Up Beach Tent with the sun/shade movement so I don't have to 1. get out of the shade and 2. it seems lighter and easier than unscrewing the umbrellas out of the sand and moving them 2+ times as we often do.

In the end, this seems like a nice option and we are happy to have it. It should work - again, will update if that doesn't happen - and we are happy to have something that already seems very easy to use. Very pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Old Bahama Bay Pop Up Beach Tent, Portable Shade Sun Shelter UPF50+ UV Protection for 4 Person Extendable Floor for Fishing Hiking Camping, Waterproof Windproof(Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
Lezyne Micro Floor Drive HP/HPG Bicycle Portable Floor Pump, Road, Gravel Bike, High Pressure, ABS Flip Chuck, Presta/Schrader I'm torn between four and five stars.

Pros: this pump is carefully engineered and obviously high quality. The gauge is accurate and easy to use. It mounts to the frame unobtrusively. It isn't very heavy considering its form and function. Where other mini pumps struggle to get road tires up to full pressure, this has no problem. It's almost a work of art and I actually look forward to my next flat tire!

Cons: The pump handle could be a bit wider; I found it hurt my hand a bit to keep pumping at higher pressures. The frame mount seems a bit flimsy (the one from my PDW pump was much more substantial) and I don't like the velcro strap--it's a bit fiddly to get the pump securely attached while the hose is secured over the handle. As I was approaching 90 psi I found I had to be careful to keep the pump stable as it required a fair bit of force to keep pushing air into the tire. I'm concerned that I may someday crossthread the hose into the base by being clumsy or in a hurry.

Overall, a well designed and executed mini pump that's different than the typical hand pump. I would buy it again, but if I could, there's a few things I would change about it.
text_fidelity_b: Lezyne Micro Floor Drive HP/HPG Bicycle Portable Floor Pump, Road, Gravel Bike, High Pressure, ABS Flip Chuck, Presta/Schrader

The price was right and the quality seems good. I like the fact that it is covered with a rubbery material that keeps it from scratching my bike.

The mount for the bike is fine but its a bit of effort to get the cable secured with the lock in such a way that it does not interfere with riding. On my bike I have a basket and usually throw the lock in the basket in transit so this is not such a problem for me.

We bought two of these locks. One for me and one for my partner. He dropped the key for his in the water beside our boat at the dock which means he is down to one key.

I saw this lock on sale on Amazon the other day for about $20 but did not order another one like I should have. If it goes on sale again Ill get my partner another lock and use his old one to lock a shopping cart to the door handle of one of those people who take up two parking places to protect their beautiful cars from the unwashed masses. For this alternative application a spare key, or even one key, would not be necessary.

Update October 9: As I mentioned above my partner dropped one of the keys for his lock into the water beside our boat. When the folks at Via Velo read my review they immediately contacted me for my mailing address and the key code. They shipped spare keys, from China, for his lock. They work fine. I had the new keys in less than a week so now we don't have to worry about breaking out the hacksaw if my partner dropped his remaining key in the drink.

In the time since I wrote my original review I have used this lock dozens of times and when I lock my bike at the gym I look at the other bikes with the $100 locks on them and cant see the difference between those and my Via Velo lock. When you add to the quality of the product the obvious commitment to customer service this company has, I am enthusiastic about what other products these folks might offer.

text_fidelity_a:
GymPaws Real Leather Hand Pad Workout Glove Alternative | Hygienic n' Washable | Slightly Padded Palm w 4 Finger Loop SweatProof Back | Mens | Womens I gave up gloves about 10 years ago in favor of pads/grips. It felt odd at first, but after a few weeks, I realized that I could never go back to using gloves. Gloves were bulky, bunched in the wrong places, and made my hands too sweaty and hot. Pads/grips gave me protection without adding bulk, were easy to take on and off when necessary, and held up longer. The only thing I didn't like was that they had a single strap that went across the back of the hand. Even if I laced my fingers through the strap, I could never get a firm enough hold to keep them on for things like medicine ball work. Everything else -- dumbbells, barbells, rowing, push ups -- was fine. So when I lost those grips, I ordered GymPaws because I thought that the individual finger loops would make for a solid grip.

Unfortunately, the GymPaws weren't a good fit for me. On three of the four finger loops, I could see daylight between my fingers and the material -- not a lot but enough that I felt the pads sliding when trying to do some fast work with the medicine ball. So GymPaws were too big for my fingers, yet they were also too small for my palms. I'm a woman, about 5'2", and my hands are proportional to my size, though obviously smaller than many other people's hands. The brand I used before GymPaws provided more coverage on the palm, but the GymPaws left a bit too much skin exposed at the base of my thumb. It didn't prevent me from getting a solid grip on the dumbbells, barbell, or rower, but it was often irritating.

Making a product like this has got to be difficult because you can only make so many sizes and still keep the price affordable. Having one size only is the easiest way, but then it's, 'One size fits all, some better than others.' For something like this, I think the only way to know is to order them and try them out for yourself.

Although I didn't like the product, I've got nothing but praise for their customer service. The return window is only 14 days, but you can return them even if they've been used. That's exactly what I did and I got my refund as soon as they received the package. Given that, I'd say that it's worth giving GymPaws a try. They didn't work for me, but they seem to work for a lot of people. Although I only had them a short time, they felt sturdy and well-made enough to last a while. But try them on every sort of gear you regularly use before the return window shuts, especially if you're transitioning from regular gloves.
text_fidelity_b: GymPaws Real Leather Hand Pad Workout Glove Alternative | Hygienic n' Washable | Slightly Padded Palm w 4 Finger Loop SweatProof Back | Mens | Womens

text_fidelity_a: Wenzel Blue Jay 25 Degree Sleeping Bag I love these bags! Got two of them to zip together for a queen sized air mattress. First off, they are big and roomy. They're big even when packed in their included "stuff sack" - slightly bigger than a water cooler bottle. They are also extremely comfortable and I have no doubt they will be warm down to 25 degrees. But nicely, they don't get too warm either. The zipper can be opened from either end, and has a velcro flap at the top to keep it from coming unzipped during the night. Zippers work great and two zip together perfectly. The only reason they didn't get 5 stars is due to the elastic bands to hold it rolled up and the stuff sack. The elastic bands are sewn to the bag and I've had them before on other bags. After a couple of years, they lose their elasticity and are useless. Attached compression straps would be much better. The stuff sack is a little bit too lightweight to last very long and the seams are not reinforced, so it won't be long before it becomes torn up. text_fidelity_a:
Thule Raceway Pro Trunk Bike Rack This is clearly a sturdy, well constructed bike rack. There's no reason to fear that it will come loose on long trips.

Unlike most other bike racks it uses tight ratcheting cables for mounting to your car instead of fabric straps. Does that make a difference? Probably not. I've had a Saris Bones rack for over two years with about 1,000 miles on it -- I've never had a problem with it.

Unlike the Saris Bones it does not have side straps (just top and bottom of the trunk). But, more of the rack's surface area is pressed against your car, so the side straps are probably less necessary.

Mounting to your car: Very simple. Once you get the hang of it, it will maybe take 2 or 3 minutes. And it's a one man job.

While it should be able to fit on practically any kind of car, before buying you should still consult Thule's website to confirm that it will fit on your car. They have a very long list of cars that it has been rated to fit onto.

Attaching your bikes: Also very simple. It takes just seconds.

As for the "patented No-Sway Cage prevents bike-to-bike contact," yes it works, but plenty of other bike racks are built to prevent mounted bucks from swaying into each other.

Storage: It folds up flat, so it doesn't take up too much space in your trunk.

Competition: Thule's major rival in the field of bike racks is Saris. I don't think you can go wrong with the Thule, but to some degree it feels over engineered. Saris' design is much simpler, and significantly cheaper (though the Saris is hardly a budget rack). The only advantage I'd give the Thule over the Saris is its ability to quickly fold flat. So I'm taking a star off because I feel that price is unnecessarily high -- you can get the same level of performance from the Saris at a lower price.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Raceway Pro Trunk Bike Rack

There was a slight breeze when we set up ours at the beach and once we had one side set up the other side fell down. All we could do was laugh and keep trying, until we really figured this thing out. Definitely stick the poles into the sand as much as you can. Also, fill the bags up with as much sand as possible and move those away from the tent as far as you can stretch them.

I absolutely love how light weight the entire tent is, and how easy and quick it is to take down! This is being added permanently to our beach gear.

text_fidelity_a: TR Foldable Camping Chair Hard Arms, Portable Lawn Chair for Adults,Outdoor Chairs Heavy Duty with Mesh Backrest Cup Holder,Support to 300LBS (Camo) I recently got another camp chair from this same company, which we really liked. But when I saw this TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm I decided to grab it because we like the first one so much. We liked the quality, the material, and how nice it feels when sitting. I actually thought this one was going to open/close the same, but missed the design in the product page photos. No worries though - while it opens like so many chairs on the market now, I usually don’t like the style as almost all of the ones I’ve tried hurt across the back of my legs. I’m a shorter guy and they tend to dig into the back of my legs. Not with this TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm - I was pleasantly surprised. When it first arrived I thought I’d blown it, but thrilled to find out I hadn’t - it actually feels great sitting on. Also unlike the other one from this same company, this one does not sit straight up, with a more reclined position. It won’t be as easy to sit at a table and eat, but for relaxing it’s going to be great. Very easy to open and close, the set up of the TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm is as quick as can be. And can set up either fully open, or partially (almost fully) collapsed, making it easy to close and move, or set around waiting to go back into the included bag. The materials are great - thick, the canvas material feels great to sit on. There is a leather (or more likely, leather-like) arm material that also feels nice. Overall, the feel and durability both seem on the spot. I think we’re going to get a lot of years and use out of both chairs. The other one we have has the side table - which is great, but we can set the two next to each other, share the side table, and this one has a pouch on each side - not lined for keeping things cool, but the same material as the chair. Keep your phone, flashlight, keys, or drink in there. The bag fits like the all do and as most do, you’re likely going to need two people to get it in. I was able to get it out on my own no issue, but to hold that bag - which is “tight,” you’re likely better off with an extra set of hands. In the end, we like this TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm as much as the first chair we got from TR, and are thrilled to have added this one. They’re going to be great for camping, the beach or park, and even out back on nice evenings.

Duluth Pack Duluth Minn Everyday Travel Gym Market Duffle Bag Pack | Gym Sports Bag Airplane Luggage Carry-On Bag - Brown I haven't had this gym duffel for very long, but since there aren't any reviews yet I figured I should offer one. This is the most money I've ever spent on a gym bag, but I took the plunge for various reasons. One being that my last two gym bags fell apart after a few years and this bag comes with a lifetime guarantee. And boy- after receiving it and feeling the nice thickness of the canvas and just how well made this thing is I must say that I definitely see this bag being able to go through hell and back for a lifetime without ever needing replacement.

Another reason I got it was for the separate base compartment in the bottom. I had a gym bag of lesser quality that had this and honestly I don't understand why more bags don't have it. It's a fantastic extra- because it keeps things completely separated from the rest of the bag. Some might say- Well, LOTS of bags have a separate compartment to put your shoes or whatever in... but I say no. Almost all bags their seperate compartments are designed in such a way that they actually take up space in the regular compartment of the bag. When you have a gym bag that has a pocket on the sides (like most do) once you fill it, the main compartment of the bag now has less space because the bulge is moving into the main compartment area. But bags with a base compartment like this one don't have this problem. You can fill the bottom compartment up without it getting in the way of anything you might have to reach for in the main compartment and without compromising any of its inside space. Really convenient. When I go to martial Arts class I can put my uniform and pads in the base compartment without ever having to deal with them throughout the day when I'm rummaging through the main compartment looking for basic things like my wallet etc. The full measurement of the bag is about 12" high/14"wide/11"deep (I did not have the bag filled up while measuring so my estimate might be slightly off) It has leather detailing on the handles for extra comfort. Duluth Pack has an even larger bag similar to this one made large enough to fit tall boots in the base compartment. I think it's called the Duluth boot duffel. That one was too large for my needs, but it might be ideal for those who need to carry more equipment.

Made in the USA... finally something NOT made in China. Excellent quality. Thick strong Zippers that do not look like they could ever break, that also zip easily. Comes with a lifetime guarantee.
text_fidelity_b: Duluth Pack Duluth Minn Everyday Travel Gym Market Duffle Bag Pack | Gym Sports Bag Airplane Luggage Carry-On Bag - Brown

text_fidelity_a: Water Bottle with Fruit Infuser and Carrying Handle 27 Ounce NO BPA (Yellow) This water bottle has some definite pros and cons. Lets start with the good: for sure it's great to be able to drink fruit infused water! I don't drink any sodas or sugary drinks, so this is a great idea. The bottle is also very pretty (i got the yellow) and it's really awesome to see my yellow top with my yellow lemon slices in the bottle. It's also nice that the fruit is contained in the inner tube and not able to come out when poured. There is also a nice flip top with a handle so it can be clipped onto a bag or just carried by the little top handle. Thats about all the good points. The unfortunate problem with this bottle is that it doesn't allow you to drink all the water in the bottle! Because of where the holes are to let water in, it prevents you from finishing your last 2 inches of water. So thats a problem because if i want to finish my water i have to take the whole top off and then the wet tube with the fruit drips everywhere and it's just awkward. You also cant fill the bottle with water all the way up because the tube of fruit displaces so much of the water. Then on top of it, when you have drank about half of the bottle, the water isn't even touching the fruit anymore! Plus, when you go to drink it, it's hard to get any water out because the fruit from the tube bumps up against the water hole and blocks it. The water will come out but only a little bit, it's very obstructed. Then we have the problem of the flip top itself. It does seal well, however in order to open the top to drink it, you have to pinch your finger under this brittle plastic piece to open it. I feel like it's very difficult to open and hurts my finger. I also feel like it's so brittle its only a matter of time before it breaks. So, overall I don't see myself continuing to use this bottle. It doesn't hold much water and doesn't function very well. I did receive this product at a discount in exchange for a review and I always give my honest opinion.
text_fidelity_b: Water Bottle with Fruit Infuser and Carrying Handle 27 Ounce NO BPA (Yellow)

text_fidelity_a:
Light & Motion Vis 360 Plus Bike Helmet Light I commute by bike and I'm obsessed with seeing and being seen at night. I have a 650 lumen TerraLUX TT-5 flashlight (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B009WFA4KU/) strapped to my handlebars as my primary light. I added this helmet-mounted light set as redundancy / extra security. I've had it about a month now.

This is a pretty good light. It's fairly bright, and I like that it has amber LED's on both sides of both the front and rear light. This makes you visible from any angle (hence the "360" in the name). Having gotten used to the blinding, virtual daylight of the 650 lumen flashlight on my handlebars, the 250 lumens that this light puts out on max doesn't seem quite bright enough to me. But I could get home safely with this alone if my flashlight were to fail, so it's bright enough.

Things I like about helmet-mounted lights in general:
1) You can aim the light wherever you need it. It's handy for checking out turns before you've made the turn. And I can now see the display from my bike computer without having to wait for a streetlight! And when I'm off my bike, I can see my lock, into my trunk bag, etc.
2) They increase visibility and therefore safety.
3) You'll probably leave them mounted to your helmet most of the time, so you're less likely to forget them. And if you're locking your bike up somewhere you'll probably take your helmet with you, so you'll automatically take your lights too - less chance of theft.

Things I like about this light in particular:
1) It's one of the brighter ones available.
2) It actively aims LED's in every direction, making you highly visible.
3) It's rechargeable and charges via USB.

Things I don't like about helmet-mounted lights in general:
1) They add weight to your head / neck.
2) They can get knocked around. I take my bike on the train for a portion of my commute, and when we near my stop I have my helmet on and am ready to get my bike out of the rack to disembark; meanwhile other riders are trying to get to their bikes. I frequently bang one or the other of the lights on the overhand above the bikes while we're all jostling around. Also, when I take my helmet off I feel I have to be more careful about stowing it so the lights don't get knocked about.

Things I don't like about this light in particular:
1) It's surprisingly heavy, and it's unbalanced. The front light is virtually weightless. The rear light, which has the battery pack, is surprisingly heavy. I invested in a very nice, "barely there" helmet that weighs virtually nothing. This light makes it feel like a brick. Obviously it's not that heavy, but it is heavier than I expected. And I don't like that all the weight is to the rear. This is okay when I'm leaning forward in riding position, but when I'm stopped at a light or otherwise upright, the weight is pulling my head back.
2) I find the rubberized button to turn it on / change modes difficult to feel and manipulate while I'm riding. If I don't take the train home, my commute is an hour and 15 minutes. To save battery I have it on low when I'm riding on well-lit streets and switch to high otherwise. I've had this light almost a month and I'm not getting better at feeling / adjusting the light. It takes concentration away from riding while I fiddle with it.
3) The tail light mode is not adjustable. It does this odd, slow fade-in / fade-out and that's it. You can't make it be always on, and you can't make it actually flash.
4) You can't have just the taillight on. Once the headlight's on, you can turn the taillight off independently, but you can't ride with just the taillight.
5) The battery is not replaceable. My flashlight / headlight runs on a replaceable, rechargeable battery, which means I can keep a spare battery in my pouch and be sure I have enough battery to get home. I can also ride with one battery while the other's at home recharging. With this light, if the battery runs out you can't use the light until you get to a USB charger. And it takes a good few hours to recharge, so you can't go riding for the hours it takes to recharge. And the low battery indicator is tucked away at the bottom of the taillight, and is only visible after you've plugged it in to recharge, so that doesn't help. So you'd better keep it charged.
6) You can change the angle of the front light, but only in discrete clicks. Each click is a very small angle of change on the device, but changes where the light hits the road by about 20'. I frequently want the light right in between two of the clicks and I can't put it there.
7) The helmet mounts strike me as odd. The front light slides into it's mount and clicks in place, but it slides in from the bottom. That means the if the clicky thing ever fails the light will slide out. If it slid in from the top gravity would keep it in place. And the rear light presses on with four tabs clicking into four slots. You really have to pull on it to dismount it. Odd.

Hmmm. Looking at this review there are way more things in the "don't like about this light" section than elsewhere, which makes it seem like I don't like this light. That's not true. None of the "don't likes" are show-stoppers. I'm keeping the light and I do like it. They're mostly just areas where I feel like the light could be somewhat better. If you buy this light you'll definitely be seen, you'll see where you're going, and you'll probably be happy you have it. These are just my observations for whatever they may be worth to you.
text_fidelity_b: Light & Motion Vis 360 Plus Bike Helmet Light

Danielson unisex-adult Anchor Pulley Gray One Size I installed one of these on each end of an Old Town Pack canoe.

For installation, I cut a small board to act as platform for the pulley that I mounted onto the canoe. Then attached the pulley onto the board. This was necessary so the pulley would hang out over the end of the canoe enough.

The installation was easy enough with the screws received with the pulleys. But, I purchased separately 1/4" brass screws with nuts as I don't think the small screws would hold for long term. Not really a criticism.

But, the pulley has a restraining device that works very well, if your anchor rope is at least 1/2" diameter. Smaller cord I am using (purchased from Amazon with a Yak Gear Nylon Rope) will not restrain when you release the cord trying to hold the anchor in place. Must instead use cleats to hold the rope, which is difficult when you pull up the anchor and it is dangling off the end of the canoe. I have a 5# mushroom anchor on either end and that is significant weight to tie off.

Not sure this is the final solution with these pulleys and the nylon rope and I may have to go back to using larger diameter rope. Really did not want to do this as this would put more rope cluttering up the canoe when I fish.

These are well made metal anchors. Just not sure about for canoe/yak applications unless you can deal with the additional mass of rope in the boat.

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. Just make sure you get the one like this one from "TLG8," to get the high quality one I just described. Thanks for reading my review. Hope it helped someone.
